m1-thread-cap.title: Cap torch/BLAS threads unconditionally at top of run.py + regression test
m1-thread-cap.imperative: In src/evo_predictor/run.py, insert immediately after the stdlib imports (argparse/json/logging/os/re/sys/dataclasses/datetime/pathlib/typing) and before `import numpy as np` / the `from src.compound_prior...` block: (1) os.environ.setdefault for OMP_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS to '1'; (2) a guarded `try: import torch; torch.set_num_threads(1)` / `except Exception:` block mirroring src/utils/utilization.py's init_worker guard style (comment convention matched from that file). Unconditional -- no isatty()/headless-detection gating (Pre-Ruling #2). Add a new unit test (tests/unit/evo_predictor/test_run_entrypoint_thread_cap.py or an addition to test_run_cli_defaults.py) asserting the entrypoint caps threads: import src.evo_predictor.run fresh and assert torch.get_num_threads() == 1 (or assert the env vars if a true fresh-process reimport isn't practical -- state which was picked). Test-after is allowed per handoff Test Mode, so this item collapses to the single green postcondition (c2) -- no separate TDD-red attest needed.
